correct: Since a divides b, b = ak for some integer k.
Since b divides c, c = bm for some integer m.
wrong: Since a divides b, b = ak for some integer k.

correct: Then x ∉ A ∪ B, so x ∉ A and x ∉ B.

wrong: Then x ∉ A ∪ B, so x ∉ A or x ∉ B.

correct: n^3 - n = (n - 1)n(n + 1), a product of three consecutive integers.
One of any three consecutive integers is divisible by 3.
wrong: n^3 - n = (n - 1)n(n + 1), a product of three consecutive integers.
One of any two consecutive integers is even.
mistake: an even factor gives divisibility by 2, not 3

wrong: Let ε > 0 and let x be a real number.
Let δ = ε / (|x + 1| + 1), and suppose |x - 1| < δ.
mistake: δ is chosen after x and depends on it: the quantifier order is wrong

correct: Let x, y with f(x) = f(y).
If x < y then f(x) < f(y), a contradiction; if y < x then f(y) < f(x), a contradiction.
wrong: Let x, y with f(x) = f(y).
If x < y then f(x) < f(y), a contradiction.
mistake: the case y < x is never ruled out
